statement: * The C_ChatInfo.SendAddonMessage function now more aggressively throttles all addon traffic on a per-prefix level. See Addon messaging changes for more details.
decision: Retail prefix registration/throttled message producer absent. Need per-prefix allowance/refill and instance/whisper exception, not Forever outbound acceptance.

statement: * The TextStatusBar FrameXML utility has been converted to a mixin. Global functions are retained for compatibility, but will be removed in Patch 11.0.0.
decision: Cached mixin/deprecated wrapper loading is a candidate; retained globals versus later 11.0.0 removal requires full cached handler/event tests. No Blizzard edit.

statement: * The loading of deprecation scripts is now controlled by a new loadDeprecationFallbacks CVar. This CVar defaults to 1 (enabled), and will reset to the default state upon a client restart.
decision: Sweep proves default/publication only. Reset across client restart and load suppression with value 0 need process-lifetime/cache-load proof; cached wrappers remain untouched.

statement: * The client now emits a Lua warning for a "Duplicate File Load" if an addon loads the same file multiple times in its TOC or XML files.
decision: No Duplicate File Load warning producer found in simulator source. Requires repeat TOC/XML loads and observable diagnostic at the loader boundary.

statement: * (May 16 2024) The C_AddOns.DisableAddOn function can no longer be used to disable secure Blizzard addons.
decision: DisableAddOn protects only __BuiltIn by folder name; that is not a secure Blizzard addon classification/permission gate. Need explicit secure ownership/loading provenance and rejection tests.

statement: * Each registered prefix is given an allowance of 10 addon messages that can be sent.
decision: 10-message capacity per registered prefix has no retail bucket state/test; declaration/enum existence does not establish capacity.

statement: * Each message sent on a prefix reduces this allowance by 1.
decision: Each send decrement requires registered-prefix bucket mutation and independent-prefix tests; no explicit retail send producer.

statement: * If the allowance reaches zero, further attempts to send messages on the same prefix will fail, returning Enum.SendAddonMessageResult.AddonMessageThrottle to the caller.
decision: Zero-allowance rejection must return exact AddonMessageThrottle enum. Enum publication alone does not establish throttled rejection.

statement: * Each prefix regains its allowance at a rate of 1 message per second, up to the original maximum of 10 messages.
decision: 1-message/second refill capped at 10 needs deterministic clock and per-prefix tests; outbound logs have no native-rate parity claim.

statement: * This restriction does not apply to whispers outside of instanced content.
decision: Out-of-instance whisper exemption requires instance state/channel-sensitive policy and tests; no retail native-throttle producer.

statement: This restriction does not mean that the global communications throttle is removed. If too much data is being sent simultaneously on separate prefixes, then the client may still be disconnected. For this reason, it is strongly recommended to continue using ChatThrottleLib or AceComm-3.0.
decision: Global disconnect throttle is explicitly separate from per-prefix allowance; no simulated transport/disconnect policy. ChatThrottleLib/AceComm recommendation is retained source context, not implemented behavior.

statement: Due to the way that the deprecation wrapper for these APIs has been handled, the C APIs are replaced by Lua functions that shift the enum result to the second return position. decision: Cached wrapper enum-return shifting needs exact first/second/last return tests with deprecation loading on/off; no retirement/deletion of wrapper. Negative select example is not a proof of C API behavior.
Preserve example literally; select(-1, ...) last-return semantics do not establish a retail C_ChatInfo enum return producer or wrapper parity.
